0.1.3.title: Drag that lands, tempo you can correct, and in-app updates
0.1.3.summary: Dropping a track onto a collection now goes where you point it, the BPM is editable by hand, and Keystone can finally update itself.
highlights: Dragging tracks to a collection lands on the row you are pointing at, and shows the key, energy and tempo of what you are carrying while you drag.
Correct a BPM by hand, with halve and double for tracks read at the wrong octave. It survives re-analysis, like the key and energy overrides.
In-app updates work. Version 0.1.0 could not check for them at all, so this one has to be installed by hand — after that Keystone updates itself.
Filing a batch of tracks no longer fails outright when one of them has been removed from the library since you listed it.
Fixed a 'database is locked' error that could make filing tracks fail while a scan was running.
Keystone's library can now be read and edited by an AI assistant that speaks MCP: search, overrides, collections, tags, renaming and export.

0.1.0.title: First release
0.1.0.summary: Keystone reads your track library, shows key, tempo and energy on a Camelot wheel, and writes what it finds back to your files.
highlights: Camelot wheel: pick a key and the library narrows to it and to everything that mixes with it.
Key, tempo and energy on every row, with cue markers you drag on the waveform.
Where a key is genuinely ambiguous, Keystone shows both candidates instead of guessing a letter.
Write key, energy and tempo into your tags or your filenames, with a preview first and an undo after.
Send cue points to rekordbox and Traktor. Your collection is backed up before anything is written.
Collections, ratings, bulk tag editing and search across the whole library.
Import playlists from the Music app, or from any .m3u.
Everything runs on your machine. No account, no uploads.
